tool_input.command:
cat > <repo>/.tmp/pr-harness.md <<'EOF'
A repeatable, dev/CI-parity test tier over `beadle-daemon`'s mail-triggered pipeline. Closes beadle-gi5t and beadle-gc0m.

## Why

That pipeline — email → trust classification → per-contact permission → planner → executor → runner → `ethos mission create` → worker spawn — had never actually run until a manual live test. That single run surfaced four real defects, including a mission-contract shape ethos's real schema rejects outright, which would have failed *every* daemon-triggered mission. Nothing automated could have caught it, because nothing exercised the path.

This is that ability.

## The constraint everything else follows from

No environment-dependent branches. **No `t.Skip` on a missing dependency** — the test fails naming what to install. One entry point: it runs under `make check`, and CI invokes that same target. No build tag, no `-tags=integration`, no CI-only invocation.

A test that silently skips locally is the same failure as one that skips in CI. That is precisely how the contract-schema bug went uncaught, so the tier must not reproduce it.

## Four gates, each with a negative case

| Gate | Positive | Negative |
|---|---|---|
| Trust classification | verified/trusted message creates a pipeline | unsigned message from an `rwx` sender creates nothing |
| Per-contact `x` permission | granted sender's verified message runs | `rw-` sender's verified message unlocks nothing |
| Command-file signature | owner-signed file loads | unsigned, wrong-key, expired-key all rejected |
| Contract validity | generated contract accepted by the **real** ethos CLI | malformed contract asserted rejected |

Gate 4's negative control is the one that matters most and is easiest to get wrong. It exists to catch a *systemic* harness failure — a `PATH` misconfiguration, a swallowed Go-side error — that would make every `ethos mission create` spuriously succeed regardless of input. Without it, gate 4's only assertion is success, which a broken harness satisfies trivially.

## What is real and what is faked

`Spawner` is the **only** faked seam. Everything else is the real component: in-process IMAP/SMTP via `testserver.Fixture`, ephemeral GPG keyrings, real signature verification, and a real `ethos mission create` exec.

The `Poller` is bypassed deliberately, not worked around. Its first poll never fires the new-mail callback and its minimum interval is 1m, so a pre-commit test cannot wait on it — and it has no security-relevant logic of its own. The gates all live in `OnNewMail` and downstream, so driving that directly is testing the right layer.

## Verification — every negative case proven able to fail

Each gate's negative case was confirmed to fail when the guard it tests is disabled, then reverted:

- Gate 1 — patched `handler.go:162` to `if false`: *"should have 0 item(s), but has 1"* on spawner call count.
- Gate 2 — disabled `perm.Execute`: same failure shape.
- Gate 3 — broke `signature.go`'s `NO_PUBKEY` case: wrong-key subtest failed.
- Gate 4's control — restored the deleted `evaluator.handle`: `require.Error` had nothing to catch.

This was not ceremony. Three of the most valuable findings in the work leading here were **tests that could not fail while being green**: a tautological assertion propping up a no-lock claim, a clock-injection test that rotted by calendar into passing under both clocks, and a CI check comparing a binary to itself.

Isolation verified separately: `~/.punt-labs/ethos` byte-identical across a full `-race` run. That tree has been corrupted by tests in this repo before.

## Two deviations from the write-set, both forced

`internal/testenv/daemon.go` as specified is impossible — `internal/daemon`'s white-box tests import `testenv`, so daemon fixtures inside `testenv` create an import cycle (`go vet`: `import cycle not allowed in test`). Hence a new `internal/daemontest` package, holding only `SignCommand` and `FakeSpawner` — the two members that genuinely need `daemon` types. For the same reason `harness_test.go` is `package daemon_test`.

Both were surfaced in the mission's `open_questions` rather than absorbed silently.

## Honesty items

`docs/TESTING.md` originally shipped an unscoped "No `t.Skip`, ever" rule while four `t.Skip("gpg not installed")` sites remained in the very package the tier covers — in a file the same document cites as gate 3's authority. Those are now converted (at the `gpgBinary` helper, once, not four times), along with a fifth in `runner_test.go`. `internal/daemon` now has **zero** `t.Skip`/`t.Skipf` call sites.

The rule is stated as the repo-wide standard with the outstanding gap cited rather than narrowed — narrowing would read as "`t.Skip` is fine elsewhere by policy," when it's fine elsewhere only because nobody has fixed it yet. Remaining sites in `internal/pgp` and `internal/email` are tracked as **beadle-hi4n**.

That bullet originally claimed "eleven" such sites. The real count is 39. The figure originated in the design doc, survived two evaluator rounds, and was relayed twice more before anyone counted. It is now stated as the file list plus the reproducing command, with **no number at all** — a corrected static count decays exactly the way the original did.

`make check` green. Test count 595 → 597 top-level tests.
EOF

tool_input.message:
The tier's first CI run failed — and it caught a genuine dev/CI divergence **in the harness itself**. Fix on `feat/daemon-test-harness`, commit, don't push.

**The failure** (run 33353470073, `test` job):

```
--- FAIL: TestBuildStageContract_ValidatesAgainstRealEthosCLI
  ethos mission create rejected the generated contract:
  ethos: mission create: unknown mission type "implement"; available archetypes:
--- FAIL: TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd/all_four_gates_pass
  "[]" should have 1 item(s), but has 0
```

Note `available archetypes:` is **empty**.

**Root cause.** `IsolateEthos` symlinks the global archetypes tree from `$HOME/.punt-labs/ethos/archetypes` into the scratch home. I verified: my machine has it (`implement.yaml`, `design.yaml`, `review.yaml`, …); the repo has no `.punt-labs/ethos/archetypes/` at all; a clean CI runner has no global ethos install. So the symlink dangles, ethos loads zero archetypes, and every generated contract is rejected because it resolves to the default `implement` type.

That is **ambient developer state** — the exact thing the design named as a hard constraint to eliminate. The tier passed locally only because I happen to have a global ethos tree.

Worth saying plainly: this is the tier working. Its first CI execution found a real environment dependency that local runs structurally could not. kth predicted this class in round 1 of the design review — *"isolatedEthosEnv assumes the global archetypes directory exists… common in CI/clean envs"* — and it was noted without being closed.

**The fix, and the part that matters most.** Materialize a minimal archetype set into the scratch tree instead of symlinking the global one. The files are tiny — the real `implement.yaml` is eight lines:

```yaml
name: implement
description: "Implementation mission — output is code"
budget_default:
  rounds: 3
  reflection_after_each: true
allow_empty_write_set: false
required_fields: []
write_set_constraints: []
```

**Always materialize — do not fall back only when the global tree is absent.** A "use global if present, synthesize if not" branch would make dev and CI run against *different* archetype data, which is precisely the divergence class this tier exists to catch. It would also mean the tier can never again detect this failure locally. Both environments must execute the identical path.

Determine which archetypes are actually needed (the contract resolves to `implement`; check whether anything else in the tier requires another) and write only those. Do not vendor the whole global tree.

**One risk to state in a comment rather than leave implicit:** a hand-written archetype can drift from ethos's real schema. That is acceptable here because the real `ethos` CLI validates it — if ethos changes the schema, this fails loudly, which is the correct outcome. Say so in the code so a future reader doesn't "helpfully" re-point it at the global tree.

Verify by reproducing CI's condition locally: run the tier with `HOME` pointed somewhere that has no `.punt-labs/ethos` at all, confirm it fails before your fix and passes after. That reproduction is the actual proof — `make check` passing on my machine is what missed this in the first place.

`make check`, commit, do not push. Report the reproduction and which archetypes you materialized.
